title: Dazzling galaxy Messier 77
caption: The barred spiral galaxy Messier 77, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: Messier 77 · constellation Cetus · about 45 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: ESO's Very Large Telescope captured Messier 77 face-on. Its glittering arms are crossed by dust lanes, giving a clear look at the structure of this barred spiral galaxy.

The calm appearance hides a more turbulent character, according to the source. The image metadata lists Messier 77 as a Seyfert galaxy, a type of galaxy with an active nucleus, a bright central region powered by material falling towards a supermassive black hole. It lies about 45 million light-years away in the constellation Cetus.

The picture was taken with the FORS2 instrument on the VLT, using visible-light filters along with a hydrogen-alpha filter that picks out the glow of hydrogen gas. In a barred spiral, the arms often begin at the ends of a bar of stars that crosses the centre.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.21 x 7.20 arcminutes) and distance (45 million light years), the frame spans roughly 94,000 × 94,000 light-years. Its light set out about 45 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: FORS2 on the Very Large Telescope observed Messier 77 through b, v and R filters plus a hydrogen-alpha filter. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
